text:
sam: heads-up — ran an nsys snapshot on the failing perf job, found a weird KV-write hotspot that lines up with fused flash-attn when batch sizes > 8. attaching perfetto link and a short trace snippet. anyone seen this before?

maria: link? can you paste the top-level timeline? quick look would help. :mag:

sam: perfetto: https://perfetto.local/trace/2942003333 (internal)

sam: snippet: `fused_flash_attn` shows repeated 1.6-2.0ms tails, kv_write kernels immediately after. KV write occupancy jumps to ~42% of step time.

alex: opened the perfetto. looks like a burst of device->device memcpys around those tails. also see a spike in `cudaMemcpyAsync` right before the write kernel.

sanjay: curious — did we change batching heuristics last week? warp occupancy + batch packing changes can shift alignment and cause bank conflicts.

jin: yes — rolled batch selector tweak in `commit 9a3f2b1` on Thursday. it increases dynamic packing for short sequences. could be related.

maria: can you run a targeted nvprof/nsys with sampling counters? I want to see L2 txn counters and shared memory bank conflicts. use: `nsys profile -o out --sample=cpu --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi` then `nvprof --print-gpu-trace --metrics l2_read_throughput,l2_write_throughput,shared_load_transactions`

sam: running now on the repro harness with batch=12, seq=512. will post output.

ops-bot: deploy/rollout: batch-selector tweak deployed to canary at 2026-03-17T09:12:45Z by jin — rollout id rlt-20260317-3

sam: nvprof excerpt:```
Device: Tesla-A100
Kernel: fused_flash_attn
Avg time: 0.78 ms (baseline) -> 1.92 ms (canary)
KV-write kernel: 0.36 ms -> 0.78 ms
L2 write transactions up 2.4x
shared_load_transactions up 1.9x
bank_conflicts detected on sm 2
```

alex: that 2.4x L2 write txn jump matches the memcpy spikes. maybe the new packing causes non-coalesced stores from KV write path.

sanjay: possible. If the fused kernel changed index ordering, the fused flash attn may be emitting KV writes with stride patterns hitting multiple banks.

maria: can you dump the kernel launch params and the pointer strides? `cupti`/`nvtx` markers around the write path would help.

sam: posted small trace with nvtx markers. launch params: `grid=(256,1,1) block=(128,1,1) shared=48KB` for fused_flash_attn; KV writer launch: `grid=(64,1,1) block=(256,1,1)`

jin: I remember adjusting chunk packing that affects per-batch sequence alignment to 32-token lanes. that would change the inner loop shape.

alex: repro idea: run two runs identical except pin batch selector to old policy. diff the perfetto timelines and nvprof counters. if the only change is packing, we isolate it.

sam: did that. results: old-policy run shows fused_flash_attn avg 0.81ms, kv_write 0.39ms, L2 writes baseline. new-policy run matches earlier numbers (1.92ms / 0.78ms).

maria: nice. So it's deterministic with the packer. Next: we should snapshot per-warp memory addresses during KV writes to confirm stride. we can add a debug build that emits first 8 pointers per warp to a small GPU side buffer and memcpy back.

sanjay: also check whether automatic prefix caching is enabled in this harness run. prefix cache writes can amplify writes when packing increases duplicated prefixes.

sam: prefix cache disabled for this repro. confirmed.

jin: patch suggestion: revert packer change for short seqs, or add an alignment pass that enforces 128B coalesced writes for KV buffers. simpler: force per-thread stride to be contiguous.

alex: I can prototype an alignment shim in the runtime that adjusts kv buffer offsets post-packing, cheap to test.

maria: while you do that, add a perf counter run with `dram_write_throughput` and `achieved_occupancy` too. if occupancy drops it's another signal.

sam: one more data point: perfetto flame shows a pattern where every 8th warp has higher latency, consistent with bank stride of 8.

ops-bot: ci/build: debug-kv-stride branch build completed — image id img-29420-debug1

alex: pushed shim to `debug-kv-stride` and testing now.

sam: quick nsight result with shim: fused_flash_attn 0.85ms, kv_write 0.41ms, L2 writes back to baseline. :tada:

maria: great — confirms packing induced non-coalesced writes. can we add a unit test in the batch selector to assert coalesced offsets for typical seq lengths?

jin: +1. I'll open a PR to add the test and a canary roll revert until we have a full fix.

sam: summary: regression introduced by packer change -> misaligned KV write strides -> L2 write txn & memcpy spikes -> fused attn tails. Repro steps, nvprof flags, perfetto link, debug shim in branch. Next: PR for runtime shim + unit test, then re-rollout.

maria: also add an eval to Redwood Optimize to detect sudden per-step L2 write jumps in smoke tests.

sanjay: nice catch team. keep trace snippets in the incident doc.

sam: thanks all. I'll file the PR and link it here.```
